source_text: Isti igitur impuri spiritus, daemones, ut ostensum a magis, a philosophis, et a Platone, sub statuis et imaginibus consecrati delitescunt, et afflatu suo auctoritatem, quasi praesentis numinis, consequuntur, dum inspirantur interim vatibus, dum fanis immorantur, dum nonnumquam extorum fibras animant, avium volatus gubernant, sortes regunt, oracula efficiunt falsis pluribus involuta. Nam et falluntur et fallunt, ut et nescientes sinceram veritatem, et quam sciunt, in perditionem sui non confitentes. Sic a coelo deorsum gravant, et a Deo vero ad materias avocant, vitam turbant, omnes inquietant, irrepentes etiam corporibus occulte, ut spiritus tenues, morbos fingunt, terrent mentes, membra distorquent, ut ad cultum sui cogant: ut nidore altarium, vel hostiis pecudum saginati remissis, quae constrinxerant curasse videantur. Hi sunt et furentes, quos in publicum videtis excurrere; vates et ipsi absque templo sic insaniunt, sic bacchantur, sic rotantur. Par et in illis instigatio daemonis, sed :ARGUMENTUM dispar furoris. De ipsis etiam illa quae paulo ante tibi dicta sunt, ut Jupiter ludos repeteret ex somnio, ut cum equis Castores viderentur, ut cingulum matronae navicula sequeretur. Haec omnia sciunt plerique pars vestrum, ipsos daemonas de semetipsis confiteri, quoties a nobis et tormentis verborum et orationis incendiis de corporibus exiguntur. Ipse Saturnus, et Serapis, et Jupiter, et quidquid daemonum colitis, victi dolore, quod sunt eloquuntur: nec utique in turpitudinem sui, nonnullis praesertim vestrum assistentibus, mentiuntur. Ipsis testibus, esse eos daemonas, de se verum confitentibus credite. Adjurati enim per Deum verum et solum, inviti miseris corporibus inhorrescunt: et vel exsiliunt statim, vel evanescunt gradatim, prout fides patientis adjuvat, aut gratia curantis aspirat. Sic Christianos de proximo fugitant, quos longe in coetibus per vos lacessebant. Ideo inserti mentibus imperitorum, odium nostri serunt occulte per timorem: naturale est enim et odisse, quem timeas; et quem metueris, infestare, si possis. Sic occupant animos, et obstruunt pectora, ut ante nos incipiant homines odisse, quam nosse: ne cognitos aut imitari possint, aut damnare non possint.
pass_a_gloss: These impure spirits, demons, as shown by magicians, philosophers, and Plato, lurk under statues and images consecrated, and by their breath gain authority, as if of a present divinity, while they inspire prophets, while they haunt temples, while they sometimes animate the fibers of entrails, govern the flights of birds, control lots, produce oracles involved in many falsehoods. For they both deceive and are deceived, so that they do not confess the true truth, which they know, to their own perdition. Thus they weigh down from heaven, and call away from the true God to material things, disturb life, disturb all, secretly penetrating even bodies, so that they create diseases, terrify minds, distort limbs, so that they may compel to their own worship: so that they may seem to have cured what they had bound, by the fumes of altars or the sacrifices of animals. These are also the raving ones, whom you see rushing out in public; prophets also rave, bacchant, and spin around without a temple. And in them is the instigation of a demon, but a different argument of madness. Also, what was said to you a little while ago, that Jupiter repeated games from a dream, that the Castors seemed to be seen with horses, that a matron's girdle followed a little ship. All these things most of you know, that the demons themselves confess about themselves, as often as they are driven out of bodies by us, by the torments of words and the fires of prayer. Saturn himself, and Serapis, and Jupiter, and whatever demons you worship, conquered by pain, speak the truth: nor indeed do they lie, especially with some of you present, about their own shame. Believe them, with them as witnesses, that they are demons, confessing the truth about themselves. For when adjured by the true and only God, they shudder involuntarily in wretched bodies: and either they leap out immediately, or they gradually vanish, as the faith of the patient assists, or the grace of the healer inspires. Thus they hastily flee from the neighborhood of Christians, whom they had long been harassing in gatherings through you. Therefore, implanted in the minds of the leaders, they secretly sow hatred of us through fear: for it is natural to hate whom you fear, and to attack whom you dread, if you can. Thus they occupy minds, and block hearts, so that men begin to hate us before they know us:

pass_b_english: These impure spirits, these demons — as magicians, philosophers, and Plato have shown — lurk beneath consecrated statues and images, and by their breath they secure authority as if a god were present, while they inspire prophets, while they haunt temples, while they sometimes animate the fibers of entrails, govern the flights of birds, control the lots, and produce oracles wrapped in many falsehoods. For they both deceive and are deceived, so that they neither know the true truth nor, knowing it, confess it to their own ruin. Thus they weigh down from heaven and call men away from the true God to material things; they disturb life, they disturb everyone, secretly penetrating even bodies like subtle spirits, so that they fabricate diseases, terrify minds, and distort limbs, in order to compel worship of themselves — so that they may seem to have cured what they themselves had bound, by the fumes of altars or by the sacrifices of fattened beasts. These are also the raving ones whom you see rushing out in public; the prophets themselves rave, bacchant, and spin about even without a temple. The instigation of a demon is the same in them, but the form of their madness differs. And you know well the things I told you a little while ago: how Jupiter ordered the games to be repeated because of a dream, how the Castors seemed to appear with horses, how a matron's girdle followed a little ship. Most of you know these things, and you know that the demons themselves confess them about themselves whenever we drive them out of bodies by the torments of our words and the fires of our prayer. Saturn himself, Serapis, Jupiter, and whatever demons you worship — conquered by pain, they speak the truth: nor do they lie about their own shame, especially with some of you standing by as witnesses. Believe them, with them as witnesses, that they are demons, since they confess the truth about themselves. For when adjured by the true and only God, they shudder involuntarily inside wretched bodies: and either they leap out immediately or they gradually vanish, as the faith of the sufferer assists or the grace of the healer inspires. Thus they flee in haste from the neighborhood of Christians, whom they had long been harassing in gatherings through you. Therefore, implanted in the minds of leaders, they secretly sow hatred of us through fear: for it is natural to hate whomever you fear, and to attack whomever you dread, if you can. Thus they occupy minds and block hearts, so that men begin to hate us before they know us.

review.notes: Pass A fails on the translation of 'ut et nescientes sinceram veritatem, et quam sciunt, in perditionem sui non confitentes'. Pass A translates this as 'so that they do not confess the true truth, which they know, to their own perdition', which implies they know the truth but refuse to confess it. However, the Latin 'ut et nescientes... et quam sciunt' (so that they [both] not knowing... and [both] the truth which they know...) indicates a dual state or a specific logical relationship regarding their ignorance and knowledge that Pass A simplifies/muddles. More critically, Pass B's translation 'so that they neither know the true truth nor, knowing it, confess it to their own ruin' is a significant departure from the Latin structure which presents two simultaneous/parallel conditions of their deception/being deceived. Furthermore, Pass A omits 'ut spiritus tenues' ('so that they [as] subtle spirits') which is present in the Latin and included in Pass B, but the omission in Pass A constitutes a loss of a descriptive clause.
reasons: Pass A omits the clause 'ut spiritus tenues' ('so that they [as] subtle spirits') found in the source 'ut spiritus tenues, morbos fingunt'.

Pass A fails to accurately capture the dual nature of the clause 'ut et nescientes sinceram veritatem, et quam sciunt, in perditionem sui non confitentes' by collapsing the 'et... et' structure into a single subordinate clause.
